question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{′}-3y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $6$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼-3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}∼{{field-1}} & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-3}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & ∼0+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\cdot (-\frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}))+{b}_{n}\cdot \frac{n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & ∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{′}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & \,-3(\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})) \\  & \,\,=-3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned} & -3\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(\frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}-3{a}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & \,\,+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}-3{b}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & \,\,\,\,=-3+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6}{{n}^{2}\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, equating the free terms and the coefficients next to sines and cosines, we obtain the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3\cdot \frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=-3 \\ \frac{{b}_{n}n\pi }{3}-3{a}_{n}=\frac{6}{{n}^{2}\pi } \\ -\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{3}-3{b}_{n}=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, ${a}_{0}=2,$ which means the constant term is given by

$$
\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}=1.
$$

Next, from the third equation, 

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{9}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation gives

$$
(-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{9})\frac{n\pi }{3}-3{a}_{n}=\frac{6}{{n}^{2}\pi }\,⇒\,{a}_{n}=-\frac{162}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+81)}.
$$

Therefore, for ${a}_{n}$ with $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =-\frac{{a}_{n}n\pi }{9} \\  & =-\frac{n\pi }{9}\cdot (-\frac{162}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+81)}) \\  & =\frac{18}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+81)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}∼1 & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{162}{{n}^{2}\pi ({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+81)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}) \\  & +{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,\frac{18}{n({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+81)}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{3}).\end{aligned}
$$
